summary: The app and the API are built, end to end, and run on one computer with stand-ins for the outside services. Everything in the first version is there: sign-up, journeys, entries with photos, clips and places, the map, following, likes, comments, Activity, search, shared journeys with invitations by link, the weekly digest, notifications, reminders, writing without a connection, reporting, blocking, a reviewer's queue, the legal pages and the web pages behind shared links. The real services (Supabase, Cloudflare R2, Mux, Expo Push, Resend, the photo check, Fly.io) each have their adapter behind a setting, ready to be switched on one at a time. Two full code reviews have been done and everything they found is fixed. What it has not had yet is a real phone and a real service: that is your part, and the next step.
next: Run it on your Mac and open it on your iPhone in Expo Go (the Run it page has the steps). After pulling the new code, run `npm ci` in `apps/mobile` once. Sign up, follow a few journeys, start one, post an entry with a photo and a place, try it without a connection. Tell me what you see and what feels wrong. The app has still never run on a real phone.

Read the calls I made while fixing the second review (Requirements, Decisions, rows 22 to 39) and tell me which you see differently. Three of them are questions I could not settle alone; they are under Open questions below.

When you are ready for real services: enrol in the Apple Developer Program first (it can take weeks, and a build of Journey on an iPhone needs it), then follow Connect the real services step by step. Each step has its own check, and the API tells you in one list what is still missing.

The first real build on a phone is the first test of everything that could only be written carefully here: push notifications arriving, Apple and Google sign-in, clips shrunk on the phone, the map on Android, the keyboard and the status bar on both kinds of phone, links that open the app.
Review the screens on the Screens page and comment on anything to change. Then confirm the accent colour (Sun for now).

open.q: One report, or several, before a journey leaves Discover?
open.a: Today one report takes a journey out of Discover, search and suggestions until a reviewer has looked (it still opens by its link). That is safe, but one person can hide a journey they dislike for a while. The alternative is to wait for reports from several different people. Which do you want for the beta?

open.q: A switch for counting in the app?
open.a: The app counts what people do (kinds and counts only, no names, nothing they wrote) when analytics is switched on in a build. There is no switch for it in Settings. The stores don't require one for this kind of counting; some people expect one. Add it?

open.q: Sentences from the API in other languages
open.a: The app's own text is now in one place, ready for translation. The sentences the API sends (errors, pushes, emails, the web pages) are English, each with a stable code. Translating those is a piece of work for when you choose a second language. Fine to leave until then?
Sun for now. Iris and Lagoon stay switchable until you have reviewed every screen.
"Journey" is taken in the app stores. Needed before the beta ends.
Microsoft's Fluent Emoji (free) are in for now. Keep them, or commission custom ones later? They can be swapped file by file.

updates.text: **The rest of the build, a second code review, and everything it found, fixed.** Your three answers are in: old comments of someone you block are removed, the API makes the small photos itself, and the tech-plan calls stand. Then the remaining features were built: places and the map, short clips, drafts that wait without a connection, push notifications and reminders, a journey that pauses itself, what's trending, moderation with a reviewer's queue, invitations by link, the legal pages, and the adapters for every real service. Five independent reviewers then read all of it as architects and found about 150 things. All are fixed or, where the fix is a product choice, written down as a call you can change (Requirements, rows 22 to 39). The ones that mattered most: a photo is now made afresh from what was uploaded and looked at before anyone sees it; nothing is lost when the API restarts in the middle of sending pushes, emails or deleting files; who may see what also holds for covers, recaps and lists of authors; every list is read from where the reader is, so it stays fast as it grows; the app opens and shows what it kept when there is no connection, and nothing you wrote is lost on the way out; and every sentence in the app is in one place, ready for translation. The docs were corrected wherever they had fallen behind the code, including one thing you should know now: **a build of Journey on your iPhone needs the paid Apple Developer Program**, because Apple doesn't sign Sign in with Apple and push notifications for a free Apple ID. Expo Go covers everything else. Tests: 256 in the API and 371 in the app, plus the browser walk-through of every screen in light and dark. None of this has run on a real phone or against a real service yet.

**A code review, and everything it found, fixed.** Defects first, each with a test: a journey made private no longer shows up for people who followed it, the owner of a shared journey hears about friends' entries, counts stay right when an account is deleted, and unexpected errors answer with a sentence instead of nothing. Then the foundation. The API has one rule for who may see what, lets the database keep the counts, sends long lists a page at a time, makes sending the same thing twice harmless, serves small photos for lists, and limits how fast one person can call it. The app is reorganised into a design system and features, takes every text size, corner and colour from the tokens (a check fails otherwise), draws only the part of a long list that is on screen, and updates what changed instead of loading everything again. A second, independent review of the new API code found six more defects, also fixed. Tests: 73 in the API (were 48), 77 in the app (were 21), and the walk-through through every screen now runs automatically on every change.

**3D icons, glass and motion.** Categories, interests, templates and empty states now use 3D icons, in the screens here and in the app. Buttons and labels on photos are frosted glass. Things you press spring back, a like makes the heart pop, progress rings fill and lists arrive one item after another; none of it moves with Reduce Motion on. Also new: Jump to, the full-screen photo viewer, loading shapes instead of spinners, and the offline banner.

**The weekly digest and share links.** "This week in the journeys you follow" opens from Activity, and every public or unlisted journey has a web page anyone can open, with a preview in chats. 48 API tests; the browser walk-through covers 61 screens and states.

**Shared journeys work.** Invite up to three people who follow you; they join only by accepting, add their own entries, and the journey shows every author. The owner stays in charge; a friend can leave at any time. 46 API tests.

**Search, settings, safety and finishing a journey.** Search for journeys and people; settings with a switch per notification, privacy, appearance and deleting your account; report and block; challenge progress; completing a journey with a closing note and its recap. The API has 44 tests, and the browser walk-through now covers 54 screens and states in light and dark.

**The core loop works end to end.** Sign-up with interests and journeys to follow, Home, the Following feed, Discover, journey pages, the story line, entries, starting a journey, posting with photos, likes, comments, creator profiles, followers and Activity. The Java API has 38 tests; a browser walk-through uses every screen in light and dark. Ten sample creators come with it and react when you post.

**Building has started.** M1, step 1: a Java (Spring Boot) API and the Expo app, sign-in with a test code, creating a profile, the tab bar, and automatic checks. Decided: **local first**, with accounts connected at the end. New page: Run it on your Mac.

**Tech stack final.** The backend is Java (Spring Boot), so you can debug it; Supabase supplies the database and sign-in. Every choice was checked against current versions and prices. New on the Tech page: how we test without the store accounts, and which account is needed when.

**Decided:** shared journeys and a weekly digest join the first version (about 15 to 17 weeks). Search-friendly pages and featured journeys come during the beta; the other ideas wait for its numbers. New screen: the weekly digest.
**Shared journeys** designed as a proposal (6 screens): friends add to one journey, and it shows on each profile. New **Engagement** page: what brings people back, what to add and when.

**59 screens in 12 groups**, from sign-in to deleting an account: login, registration, feed, discover, story line, posts, create, activity, profile, settings, safety and states. **Sun** chosen as the accent.
**The Journey Hub** replaces Figma: screens, design system, cues, inspiration, requirements, roadmap and tech in one page, built from the repo. Comment buttons added.
**Design 2.0**: real photos, bold type, glass controls, light and dark, three accent colours to choose from.
**Requirements finalized** with your eight decisions: both audiences, short video clips, worldwide in English, free with no ads.
First designs (v1) in Figma: a warm paper look. Replaced by Design 2.0 after your review.
Requirements, tech stack, roadmap and design brief written from your earlier AI discussions.
Project started, with its own cloud environment.
